required_stages.description: Allocate a fresh (n,) float16 output inside run().
One kernel pass that reads each float32 element once, converts it to float16 (round-to-nearest-even) and stores it once at the same position; no reduction, scale or clamp.

forbidden_substitutions.message: The conversion must be performed by the kernel, not by a PyTorch cast.
A host-side copy inside run() performs the conversion or an extra pass on the host.
An absmax/scale/clamp/integer-quantisation step is not part of this operator; the reference is a bare fp32 -> fp16 cast.
Returning the input or a view/cast of it replaces the whole computation.
No initialised scratch is part of this operator.

required_evidence.message: No float16 conversion target found inside the kernel.
No kernel-level store found; the conversion must be done by a kernel.

outputs.aliasing: none; the returned (n,) float16 tensor must be freshly allocated inside run() and must not share storage with x

timing_boundary.notes: Everything inside run() is timed: the output allocation, an optional no-op contiguous() guard and the single conversion kernel. No absmax or scale pass exists; no cached state; no host-side cast or copy of x.
